attribution.note: These are Zitron's own words in his own post, not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: The normalised wording matches the statement: AI is not paying for itself and keeps drawing on debt and venture capital. It is a firm statement about the present state, so observation is the right kind.

contract.note: Reading this as the industry as a whole failing to cover its costs and repeatedly needing outside financing is a fair, ordinary reading. Using the latest completed quarter is a reasonable choice for a present-tense claim. The contract also correctly separates raising money from making losses.

evidence.note: Fed working paper, published before the evaluation date. It finds the frontier labs are not consistently profitable. That covers only a few labs, not industry-wide cost coverage or dependence on financing.
IMF note. It describes highly profitable incumbent firms alongside growing reliance on outside financing. That points both ways and gives no aggregate AI-only accounts.

reviews.rationale: Neither item gives industry-wide AI revenue, costs or financing flows for Q3 2026. The Fed paper covers only lab profitability. The IMF note shows profitable incumbents alongside rising outside financing. Together they do not settle whether the industry as a whole covers its costs or depends on debt and venture money.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The claim says Huang was necessary to the AI bubble. Causal is the right kind, but the wording is heavily rhetorical.

contract.note: The speaker named no measure of the bubble or of what 'without Jensen' means. The contract tests it against what happened after Huang left. That fits the post's context, but the result depends on that chosen reading, and a five-day window cannot show whether the boom lasted.

evidence.note: Reuters report that Huang stepped down and Kress became interim CEO. It confirms the leadership change but says nothing about whether the boom continued or ended.
Investors interviewed say they doubt the boom ends just because NVIDIA slows its investing. These are expectations, not observed results, so they do not contradict the claim.

reviews.rationale: The packet confirms Huang's departure and contains opinions about what follows. It has no evidence that the boom ended, or carried on, because of his absence, and nothing separates his role from other causes. The window is also too short.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post. The figure he uses probably comes from Ramp, but he asserts it as his own claim.

semantics.note: The normalised claim keeps all the parts: the 80%/1% concentration, the 'vast majority' unprofitable startups, and the largest purchasers being NVIDIA-funded.

contract.note: He wrote 'revenues', and reading that as total revenue is fair and ordinary. Keeping Ramp's narrower sample of business spending separate from total revenue is appropriate.

evidence.note: Ramp says 80% of spend on OpenAI and Anthropic comes from 1% of firms, but only among businesses in Ramp's own data. That is not total company revenue, and the figure is undated and says nothing about who those firms are or whether they make money.
Cursor's own November 2025 announcement names NVIDIA as an investor. It backs only the funding link for one named firm, not its rank as a token buyer or its profitability.

reviews.rationale: Ramp's 80%/1% figure covers only business spending in Ramp's data, not total revenue. Nothing in the packet shows who the top 1% are, whether most are unprofitable startups, or how the named firms rank as token buyers. Only NVIDIA's funding of Cursor is documented.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Taking 'the central bank of AI' to mean NVIDIA's funding is reasonable. The claim is a vague, partly rhetorical judgement about how much support is left.

contract.note: 'Very little' and 'this entire thing' have no measure, so the result depends on the chosen reading of scope and adequacy. That reading is ordinary, but it is supplied by the evaluator.

evidence.note: Yahoo Finance, dated the evaluation day. It says NVIDIA's signed obligations are still owed and that it plans a $10B Anthropic stock purchase. That weakens the idea that NVIDIA's support vanished, but it does not measure how much other support the industry has.

reviews.rationale: Nothing in the packet shows NVIDIA withdrawing its support, or measures the industry's other funding against what it needs. The one item shows NVIDIA's commitments continuing, which only qualifies the premise. The packet does not settle the claim.
